question: Does the publicly accessible 2001 Naujan Lake stock-assessment chapter provide usable historical species or catch evidence for Bangwit's freshwater coverage?

source.title: Stock assessment of commercially important fishes in Naujan Lake
source.publication: In Conservation and Ecological Management of Philippine Lakes in Relation to Fisheries and Aquaculture, pp. 99-107
source.repository: Southeast Asian Fisheries Development Center Institutional Repository
source.access: The repository exposes a View/Open PDF. Its item page says document requests cannot be fulfilled while the publication remains for sale in print. No item-specific reuse license or public-app permission was found in the reviewed metadata.

survey.reportedSurveyFrequency: Ten sampling days per month at two-day intervals
survey.methodSummary: Actual landing observations and interviews recorded on survey forms; the study describes capture fisheries and landed catch.
survey.catchByLandingCenter: Table 4 gives monthly/annual totals by landing center but does not allocate taxa to individual centers.
survey.catchByGear: Tables 3 and 6 aggregate catch composition by gear, with several broad or inconsistently named groups.

sourceConflicts.details: The abstract summarizes 61% tilapia, 16% therapon, 4% goby, 2% mudfish and 17% other catch. The results narrative names Therapon spp. at 16% and 'pla salid' (Trichogaster spp.) at 2%, while the extracted Table 2 headings/totals place 16% under 'pla salid' and about 2% under 'gourami'. Preserve the source wording; do not silently reconcile the categories or percentages.

The chapter reports four lake landing centers, but its location table gives total catch by center rather than a taxon-by-center matrix. The chapter does not provide coordinates, voucher identifiers, or a modern occurrence record.
The data describe catches landed during 1995-1996. They do not establish current presence, abundance, recreational catchability, habitat-range boundaries, or present fishing advice.

rightsAndUse.decision: Retain only a cited research summary. Do not copy tables, figures, or full catch series into the public application unless item-specific reuse terms are confirmed.

limitations: This chapter is a historical commercial-fisheries assessment and is not a complete Lake Naujan checklist or a regional freshwater inventory.
Several reported categories are genus-level or common-name groups, and the abstract, narrative and extracted table do not agree on category labels and percentages.
The site totals are not taxon-by-landing-center data; no fish-specific collection event dates, coordinates or vouchers were recovered.
Repository access to a PDF does not establish permission to republish structured data; the item-specific license remains unverified.
No names were taxonomically normalized in this review.

sources.supports: Repository citation, authors, year, abstract, survey summary, and notice that the publication remains for sale in print; no item-specific license was displayed.
Full nine-page chapter, methods, 1996 catch tables, category labels, and their narrative/table discrepancies.

nextAction: Cross-check source spellings only after independently reviewing the chapter tables and preserve the 1995-1996 time scope. Continue MIMAROPA lake and river source discovery; do not treat these broad historical catch groups as current app species rows.
